identityReview: El Anatsui / 埃尔·阿纳祖, Ghanaian artist born in 1944 in Anyako. Birth year only; Nigerian teaching and studio practice do not establish Nigerian citizenship. Conflicting Commons creator metadata rejected.
lifeStatusEvidence: 2026 White Cube presentation of new works and September 16 Philadelphia Museum announcement describe ongoing artistic practice and collaboration. These are documentary evidence of current practice, not verified personal attendance. The announced catalogue interview was not read and its recording date is unknown.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Artist studio biography and CV, award issuer records, museum collection and exhibition records, gallery exhibition page, joint commission announcement, Art21 text description, republished profile and Commons object description.
sourceReview.scope: Identity, education and teaching, materials and collaborative process, awards, commissions, collection dates and announced exhibitions.
corrections: CV separates 1968 bachelor studies, 1969 postgraduate diploma in art education, and 1975 move to teach in Nigeria. Diploma is not a doctorate; professor rank is listed for 1996–2011. Biography prose conflates dates.
Ghanaian identity retained; Nigerian work is not a citizenship claim. Conflicting full birth dates and American creator metadata omitted.
Aluminum bottle caps and copper wire form metal sculpture resembling textiles; not woven cloth. Assistant collaboration and artist composition both acknowledged.
2015 Golden Lion is lifetime achievement at the Art Biennale, not a national pavilion or film award. 2017 Praemium Imperiale category is sculpture.
Behind the Red Moon is a 2023–2024 Tate Hyundai commission, not a competitive award; distinct from the later After the Red Moon.
Met object Between Earth and Heaven was created in 2006 and acquired in 2007, accession 2007.96.
White Cube Hong Kong venue dates are March 25–May 9, 2026; new double-sided work does not establish personal attendance.
September 16, 2026 Philadelphia announcement concerns a December 19, 2026–May 2, 2027 future exhibition; not opened by the cutoff.
Art21 description refers to filming in 2011 and publication in 2012, not a recent appearance; full film was not reviewed.
TIME100 claims not independently verified and omitted. Existing portrait candidate is a photograph of Man’s Cloth, not the person.
sourceReview.limits: AI semantic review only, without human or native-language certification. Primary institutional sources establish their own records; current exhibitions do not establish physical attendance. Unverified claims and conflicting precise birth dates omitted.

translationReview.scope: All 32 Chinese fields and seven translations checked for chronology, education versus honorary degrees, teaching rank, metal versus textile, collaborative authorship, award categories and future exhibition dates.
